profile.headline: Software Engineer at Tait
profile.summary:
As a seasoned software engineer, I thrive at the intersection of art and technology, leveraging innovative solutions to drive creative and impactful projects. My expertise spans back-end and front-end development, software architecture, embedded programming, artificial intelligence, and sound engineering. Passionate about diversity and inclusion, I actively contribute to advancing minorities in STEM through mentorship and leadership roles.

Explore my personal website with blogs and projects: https://kthomas.tech
Explore my projects on GitHub: https://github.com/kdthomas7

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developer on the iQ Navigator entertainment automation platform.

• Lead in documenting and analyzing the software architecture of iQ’s backend
• Initiated and maintain comprehensive documentation for iQ’s backend systems
• Improved performance of major user workflows by 98% using custom performance profiling tools, enhancing system efficiency and user experience
• Oversee planning work and high-level technical details for major software features
• Serve as point of contact for other developers with questions related to feature implementation and technical challenges
• Provide support for front-end development as needed, ensuring seamless integration and functionality

projects.title: Ethical Analysis of Predicting Grades with Machine Learning
projects.description: Abstract: The importance of tools that help in understanding the predictions and decisions a machine learning model makes is growing. There is a need to be able to understand the outcomes of a model and the ethical implications of it. In this paper, I analyze the quality and effectiveness of visual explanation tools provided by Yellowbrick and present a framework that can help analyze and address the ethical implications of a model. The results show that Yellowbrick did provide quality explanations that aided in understanding the models used. The explanations aligned with what social science says about the relationship between sex/gender and mathematics grades. Furthermore, I found that the ethical framework aided in analyzing ethics regarding the grade predicting model.
